DATE:  AUGUST 28, 2023
TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL
FROM:  NEIGHBORHOOD SERVICES DEPARTMENT
  EMERGENCY SERVICES
DISTRICT:  ALL
SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2023-055, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE RATIFYING THE
  DIRECTOR OF EMERGENCY SERVICES’ PROCLAMATION OF A
  LOCAL EMERGENCY RESULTING FROM TROPICAL STORM
  HILARY

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-055, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale ratifying the Director of Emergency Services’ Proclamation of a Local
Emergency resulting from Tropical Storm Hilary.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-055 ratifying the Director of Emergency Services’
  Proclamation of a Local Emergency resulting from Tropical Storm Hilary; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or their designee to negotiate and execute such
  contracts, agreements, applications or other documents with such other Federal,
  State, or local agencies or other groups and organizations as are necessary to
  obtain emergency aid, assistance, or services to the City of Palmdale.
BACKGROUND
The National Weather Service issued a Tropical Storm Warning on August 18, 2023,
warning of conditions of damage and extreme peril to the safety of persons and property
within the City of Palmdale. On Sunday, August 20, 2023, conditions of disaster or
extreme threat to persons and property were present due to Tropical Storm Hilary, which
arrived in the City of Palmdale bringing high winds and gusts, intense precipitation,
debris flow, urban flooding falling and downed trees, and adverse impacts to critical
infrastructure. The City of Palmdale received approximately six inches of rain in a 24-
hour period.
Both public and private property sustained damage. The City virtually activated the
Emergency Operation Center in response to the emergency. City Staff were deployed
 Report to the Mayor and City Council
Re: Resolution CC 2023-055
August 28, 2023
Page 2

to clear roads, alleviate flooding, and inspect damaged dwellings. In addition, Victory
Outreach opened the City Community Emergency Resource Center, providing refuge
from the storm for residents in need. On August 20, 2023, the County of Los Angeles
and the State of California each declared an emergency, both in response to Tropical
Storm Hilary.
DISCUSSION
On August 24, 2023, the City’s Director of Emergency Services proclaimed the
existence of a local emergency within the City of Palmdale, pursuant to the California
Government Code Section 8630 and Municipal Code Section 2.28.040. An emergency
proclamation issued by the Director of Emergency Services is valid for seven days and
must be reviewed and ratified by the City Council. Resolution CC 2023-055 would ratify
the Director of Emergency Services’ Proclamation of a local emergency resulting from
the Tropical Storm Hilary Incident and would authorize the Director of Emergency
Services to continue to take appropriate measures to protect public health, safety, and
welfare and obtain emergency aid from other agencies. In accordance with 2.28.040,
the Director of Emergency Services is empowered to take actions including but not
limited to obtaining vital supplies, equipment, and such other properties found lacking
and needed for the protection of life and property and to bind the City for the fair value
thereof.
FISCAL IMPACT
$1,200,000; the initial damage estimate on Monday, August 21, 2023, is $1,200,000. It
is recommended that the City Council appropriate funds from the General Fund
Emergency Reserves, in accordance with the City’s Reserve Policy.
STRATEGIC PLAN
Goal I: Maintain effective public safety and protection for life, property, and the
environment.
  B. Be prepared to protect life, property, and the environment in the event of
  catastrophic disasters and emergencies.

 Prepared by:  Arpen Shadkamyan, Emergency Services
  Administrator

   CITY COUNCIL
  CITY OF PALMDALE, CALIFORNIA
  RESOLUTION NO. CC 2023-055

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE
  THE DIRECTOR OF EMERGENCY SERVICES’ PROCLAMATION OF A
  LOCAL EMERGENCY RESULTING FROM TROPICAL STORM HILARY

  WHEREAS, the National Weather Service issued a Tropical Storm Warning on
August 18, 2023, warning of conditions of damage and extreme peril to the safety of
persons and property within the City of Palmdale; and

  WHEREAS, on Sunday, August 20th, 2023, conditions of disaster or extreme
threat to persons and property were present due to Tropical Storm Hilary, which
arrived in the City of Palmdale bringing high winds and gusts, intense precipitation,
debris flow, urban flooding falling and downed trees, and adverse impacts to critical
infrastructure; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Palmdale received approximately six inches of rain in a
24-hour period; and

  WHEREAS, the City’s Director of Emergency Services did proclaim the
existence of a local emergency within the City of Palmdale, pursuant to California
Government Code Section 8630 and Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.28.040, on
the 24th of August, 2023; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Palmdale City Council does hereby find that the
aforesaid conditions resulting from the Tropical Storm Hilary Incident warrant and
necessitate the proclamation of the existence of a local emergency by the City’s
Director of Emergency Services.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. Pursuant to Government Code Section 8630 and Palmdale
Municipal Code Section 2.28.040, the City Council ratifies the proclamation of the
Director of Emergency Services of a state of local emergency and hereby proclaims
that a state of local emergency continues to exist within the City of Palmdale.

  SECTION 2. The City Council directs the Director of Emergency Services or their
designee to take such actions as are appropriate to the fullest extent provided by the
 Resolution No. CC 2023-055
Page 2 of 2
Federal, State, and local law to protect the public health, welfare, safety, and property
of the residents of the City of Palmdale and in accordance with Municipal Code section
2.28.040.

  SECTION 3. The City Council further authorizes the Director of Emergency
Services or their designee to negotiate or execute such contracts, agreements,
applications, or other documents with such other Federal, State, or local agencies or
other groups and organizations as are necessary to obtain emergency aid, assistance,
or services to the City of Palmdale and other actions provided in accordance with
Municipal Code Section 2.28.040.

  SECTION 4. The aforementioned local emergency shall be deemed to continue
to exist until this City Council proclaims its termination. In accordance with California
Government Code 8630, this City Council shall review the need for continuing this
local emergency at least once every 60 days until it terminates the local emergency.

  SECTION 5. The City Clerk shall certify to the adoption of this resolution.

PASSED, APPROVED and ADOPTED this 28th day of August, 2023.
